@startuml PublishWorkflowVersion
title Publish Workflow Version
autonumber

actor User
boundary "Workflow Designer" as UI
control "Workflows Controller" as Controller
control "Publish Workflow Handler" as Handler
control "Node Catalog" as Catalog
database "PostgreSQL" as DB

User -> UI: Click Publish
UI -> Controller: POST /api/workflows/{workflowId}/versions
Controller -> Handler: PublishWorkflowCommand(workflowId, userId)
Handler -> DB: Load workflow, owner and draft
DB --> Handler: Workflow and draft definition

alt Workflow/draft missing or access denied
    Handler --> Controller: 404 Not Found / 403 Forbidden
    Controller --> UI: Return error
    UI --> User: Show error
else Draft is available
    Handler -> Catalog: Get node categories and config schemas
    Catalog --> Handler: Catalog metadata
    Handler -> Handler: Validate trigger, actions, catalog keys,
    Handler -> Handler: required config and graph reachability

    alt Validation failed
        Handler -> DB: Save structured validationErrors
        DB --> Handler: Errors persisted
        Handler --> Controller: 400 Bad Request + issues
        Controller --> UI: Return validation issues
        UI --> User: Group issues and highlight affected nodes
    else Validation passed
        Handler -> DB: BEGIN transaction
        Handler -> DB: Insert immutable WorkflowVersion
        Note right of DB: versionNumber = max + 1
        Handler -> DB: Update currentVersionId and workflow status
        Handler -> DB: Clear draft validationErrors
        Handler -> DB: COMMIT transaction
        DB --> Handler: New version metadata
        Handler --> Controller: Published version result
        Controller --> UI: 201 Created
        UI --> User: Show publish success and version number
    end
end

@enduml

control "Executions Controller" as Controller
control "Start Execution Handler" as Handler
collections "Executor Registry" as Registry
control "Credential Vault" as Vault
participant "Google Sheets / Gmail" as Google
database "PostgreSQL" as DB

User -> UI: Click Run on published version
UI -> Controller: POST /api/executions\n{ workflow_version_id }
Controller -> Handler: StartExecution(versionId, userId)
Handler -> DB: Check access and load version definition
DB --> Handler: Published definition

alt Version missing or caller not authorized
    Handler --> Controller: 404 Not Found / 403 Forbidden
    Controller --> UI: Return error
    UI --> User: Show error
else Version is accessible
    Handler -> Handler: Check manual trigger and linear edge chain
    Handler -> DB: Create Execution(status = RUNNING)
    DB --> Handler: executionId

    loop Nodes in directed chain: Manual -> Sheets -> Filter -> Gmail
        Handler -> Registry: Resolve executor by node.data.key
        Registry --> Handler: Node executor
        opt Node requires a credential
            Handler -> Vault: Resolve credential_id for owner and connector
            Vault -> DB: Load encrypted credential
            DB --> Vault: Encrypted secret
            Vault --> Handler: Decrypt in memory
        end
        Handler -> Registry: Execute node with input and config
        opt Google Sheets or Gmail node
            Registry -> Google: Read sheet rows or send email
            Google --> Registry: Node result
        end
        Registry --> Handler: Output or node error
        Handler -> DB: Save execution_node_log
        alt Node failed
            Handler -> DB: Set execution status = FAILED
            Note over Handler,DB: Stop traversal; remaining nodes are skipped
        else Node succeeded
            Handler -> Handler: Pass output to next node
        end
    end

    alt All nodes succeeded
        Handler -> DB: Set execution status = SUCCESS
    end
    Handler -> DB: Save finish time and duration
    DB --> Handler: Execution and node logs
    Handler --> Controller: Execution DTO
    Controller --> UI: Return result synchronously
    UI --> User: Show status and node logs
end

@enduml

@startuml WorkflowDraftPersistence
title Workflow Draft Creation, Loading and Autosave
autonumber

actor User
boundary "Workflow Designer" as UI
control "Workflows Controller" as Controller
control "Designer Handlers" as Handlers
database "PostgreSQL" as DB

User -> UI: Start a new workflow
UI -> Controller: POST /api/workflows
Controller -> Handlers: CreateWorkflowCommand
Handlers -> DB: Insert workflow metadata
DB --> Handlers: workflowId
Handlers --> Controller: Created workflow
Controller --> UI: 201 Created + workflowId

UI -> Controller: GET /api/workflows/{workflowId}/draft
Controller -> Handlers: GetWorkflowDraftQuery
Handlers -> DB: Find draft by workflowId
alt Draft exists
    DB --> Handlers: Saved definition
    Handlers --> Controller: Draft definition
    Controller --> UI: 200 OK + definition
else No draft exists yet
    DB --> Handlers: No record
    Handlers --> Controller: Not Found
    Controller --> UI: 404 Not Found
    UI -> UI: Initialize empty graph
end

loop Each graph change
    User -> UI: Add/edit/remove node or edge
    UI -> UI: Debounce autosave (~2 seconds)
    UI -> Controller: PUT /api/workflows/{workflowId}/draft\n{ definition }
    Controller -> Handlers: SaveDraftCommand
    Handlers -> DB: Verify parent workflow exists
    alt Workflow missing
        DB --> Handlers: No workflow
        Handlers --> Controller: Not Found
        Controller --> UI: 404 Not Found
    else Workflow exists
        Handlers -> DB: Upsert the workflow's single draft
        Note right of DB: Save definition as-is; invalid drafts are allowed
        Handlers -> DB: Clear stale validationErrors and update timestamp
        DB --> Handlers: workflowId, updatedAt
        Handlers --> Controller: Save confirmation
        Controller --> UI: 200 OK + updatedAt
        UI --> User: Show Saved state
    end
end

@enduml

1	Status: ready-for-agent
2	
3	## Problem Statement
4	
5	Users (Workflow Developers, Business Users, and Administrators) need a secure, intuitive, and robust way to register accounts, sign in, manage active sessions, and recover forgotten passwords. Without an email verification mechanism, malicious or mistyped email registrations can pollute the system. Furthermore, storing ephemeral one-time passwords (OTPs) in the relational database risks bloat and performance degradation, while relying on console logs or insecure mock codes compromises production security.
6	
7	## Solution
8	
9	A complete, production-grade Authentication and Authorization system for FlowPilot:
10	1. **Interactive Auth Modal**: Allows users to seamlessly toggle between Sign In, Sign Up, and Forgot Password directly within the application.
11	2. **Real-time Password Strength Meter**: Provides immediate visual feedback on password complexity (length, uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters) and confirms password match before submission.
12	3. **Redis-backed OTP Verification**: Implements a 2-step registration and password recovery flow. OTPs (6-digit numeric codes) are stored in Redis with an automatic 5-minute TTL (Time-To-Live) and deleted immediately upon successful verification, keeping the primary relational database completely clean.
13	4. **Real SMTP Email Delivery**: Sends beautifully formatted verification emails via Nodemailer with strict SMTP configuration, ensuring users receive their OTPs in their inbox without insecure UI autofill or debug log exposure.
14	5. **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Supports roles (`ADMIN`, `DEVELOPER`, `BUSINESS_USER`) embedded in signed JWT tokens, with user profile retrieval (`/me`) and secure session persistence.
15	
16	## User Stories
17	
18	1. As a Business User, I want to view an authentication modal from the navigation bar, so that I can easily sign in or register without losing my current page context.
19	2. As a Business User, I want to see real-time visual feedback on my password strength while registering, so that I can create a secure password that meets enterprise security standards.
20	3. As a Business User, I want immediate validation when my password confirmation does not match the entered password, so that I don't submit mismatched credentials.
21	4. As a Business User, I want to select my role (`DEVELOPER` or `BUSINESS_USER`) during registration, so that my account is assigned appropriate initial permissions.
22	5. As a Business User, I want to receive a 6-digit OTP in my email inbox upon submitting the registration form, so that I can verify that I own the email address.
23	6. As a Business User, I want the system to warn me if an email address is already registered before sending an OTP, so that I can choose to log in instead.
24	7. As a Business User, I want to enter my 6-digit OTP in a dedicated verification screen, so that my registration is completed securely.
25	8. As a Business User, I want the ability to request a new OTP if my current code expired or was not received, so that I am not permanently blocked from completing registration.
26	9. As a Business User, I want clear countdown and error messaging if an entered OTP is incorrect or expired, so that I understand why verification failed.
27	10. As a Business User, I want to log in using my registered email and password, so that I can access my workflows and account data.
28	11. As a Business User, I want my authentication session to persist across page reloads via a JWT token, so that I don't have to repeatedly re-authenticate.
29	12. As a Business User, I want to see my profile avatar, name, email, and role in the navigation bar when logged in, so that I know which account is active.
30	13. As a Business User, I want to securely log out with a single click, so that unauthorized persons cannot access my account on shared devices.
31	14. As a Business User, I want to initiate a "Forgot Password" flow by entering my email address, so that I can regain access to my account if I forget my credentials.
32	15. As a Business User, I want to receive a password reset OTP via email, so that only the email owner can reset the account password.
33	16. As a Business User, I want to enter the reset OTP along with my new password and confirmation, so that my password is updated in a single verified step.
34	17. As a Workflow Developer, I want to be automatically redirected or authorized based on my `DEVELOPER` role, so that I can access workflow design and debugging features.
35	18. As an Administrator, I want users' sensitive credentials to be stored as salted hashes (bcrypt) and ephemeral OTPs to be kept in memory-backed storage, so that the primary database remains clean, high-performing, and secure.
36	
37	## Implementation Decisions
38	
39	- **Architecture & Pattern**: The Monolith Backend follows Clean Architecture and CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation). The Auth feature is encapsulated into its own dedicated module, exposing clean commands and queries (`SendRegisterOtpCommand`, `VerifyOtpCommand`, `RegisterCommand`, `LoginCommand`, `RefreshTokenCommand`, `GetCurrentUserQuery`, `ForgotPasswordCommand`, `ResetPasswordCommand`).
40	- **Clean Architecture Email Decoupling**: The application layer depends on the `EmailService` domain abstraction (`libs/auth/src/domain/services/email.service.ts`). The infrastructure layer provides `NodemailerEmailService`, cleanly bound in `AuthModule`. Reusable HTML and plain-text email templates are generated via `EmailTemplateBuilder` rather than inline strings.
41	- **Storage Strategy for OTPs**: OTPs are strictly stored in Redis with a 5-minute TTL (`EX 300`). No OTP records are stored in PostgreSQL, and any legacy OTP relational tables have been removed. Keys are structured with domain namespaces (e.g. `otp:register:<email>` and `otp:reset:<email>`) and are automatically deleted upon successful verification.
42	- **Decoupled Verification**: A dedicated `POST /auth/verify-otp` endpoint validates OTPs and records verified status in Redis (`otp:verified:<type>:<email>`) with a 15-minute TTL, allowing flexible two-step registration and password reset workflows.
43	- **Refresh Token Mechanism**: 
44	  - `accessToken`: 15-minute expiration, containing `sub`, `email`, and `role`.
45	  - `refreshToken`: 7-day expiration, stored in Redis (`refresh_token:<REDACTED>`) with 7-day TTL.
46	  - `POST /auth/refresh`: Validates refresh token against Redis, verifies user active state, and issues a new access token and rotated refresh token.
47	- **Frontend HTTP Client Architecture**: 
48	  - Shared Axios instance (`frontend/src/shared/api/http-client.ts`) with request and response interceptors.
49	  - Request Interceptor: Reads `accessToken` from `auth.store` and automatically injects `Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>` on all requests.
50	  - Response Interceptor: Intercepts `401 Unauthorized` responses, calls `POST /auth/refresh` with `refreshToken`, replays failed requests with the new access token, and triggers `logout()` if refresh fails.
51	  - Migrated both `auth.api.ts` and `workflow.api.ts` to use this shared client.
52	- **Email Delivery Mechanism**: Transports OTP emails via real SMTP through `NodemailerEmailService`. Credentials (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM`) are loaded from environment variables. For local development, MailHog (`mailhog/mailhog:v1.0.1`) runs via Docker Compose on port 1025 (SMTP) and port 8025 (Web UI).
53	- **Password Security**: Passwords must meet minimum complexity criteria (minimum 8 characters, at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, 1 number, and 1 special character). Passwords are hashed using bcrypt with a salt round factor of 10 prior to persistence.
54	- **API Contracts**:
55	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/send-register-otp`: Validates uniqueness of email and dispatches a 6-digit OTP to the email address.
56	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-otp`: Accepts `{ email, otp, type }`, verifies OTP code in Redis, and marks email as verified for 15 minutes.
57	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/register`: Accepts name, email, password, role, and optional OTP. Checks verification status or verifies OTP, creates user in PostgreSQL, and issues both access and refresh tokens.
58	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/login`: Validates email and password, returning user details, `accessToken` (15m), and `refreshToken` (7d).
59	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`: Accepts `{ refreshToken }`, verifies against Redis, and returns a new token pair.
60	  - `GET /api/v1/auth/me`: Validates the Bearer <REDACTED> token and returns the current authenticated user's profile.
61	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password`: Checks user existence and dispatches a 6-digit password reset OTP to the email address.
62	  - `POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password`: Accepts email, OTP, and new password. Verifies OTP from Redis, updates the user's hashed password, and invalidates the OTP.
63	
64	## Testing Decisions
65	
66	- **Testing Seam Principle**: Tests must evaluate external behavior at the highest possible seams without testing internal implementation details or mocking CQRS internals.
67	- **Backend Testing Seam**: HTTP API Integration Tests on `apps/api` (`/api/v1/auth/*`). The test suite communicates directly via HTTP calls against running or test-instantiated NestJS application instances with real Redis and PostgreSQL test instances. Assertions verify:
68	  - HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 409).
69	  - JWT token validity, expiration, and payload contents.
70	  - Token refresh and rotation via `POST /auth/refresh`.
71	  - Redis key creation, TTL enforcement, and post-verification deletion.
72	  - User creation in PostgreSQL and password hash verification.
73	- **Frontend Testing Seam**: Component and user flow integration tests on `AuthModal`, `features/auth`, and Axios interceptors using React Testing Library. Assertions verify:
74	  - Switching between Login, Register, and Forgot Password modes.
75	  - Password strength validation bar changes color and width as characters are typed.
76	  - Form submission triggers OTP step and renders the 6-digit OTP input.
77	  - Zustand `auth.store` properly updates `user`, `token`, `refreshToken`, and `isAuthenticated` states.
78	  - Shared Axios interceptor intercepts 401 and calls refresh endpoint.
79	
80	## Out of Scope
81	
82	- Multi-factor authentication (MFA/TOTP) via authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy).
83	- Social / OAuth2 login providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft).
84	- Multi-tenant Organization/Team management (planned for post-MVP).
85	
86	## Further Notes
87	
88	- **MailHog Local Testing**: Run `docker-compose up -d mailhog` and view sent emails at `http://localhost:8025`.
89	- **Database Seeding**: `monolith-backend/prisma/seed.ts` does not run automatically on app start; it is executed manually via `npx prisma db seed`.
90	- Production deployments require valid SMTP relay credentials configured in environment variables (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM`).
91	- Redis service is managed via Docker Compose (`flowpilot-redis`).
92

Status: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

Users (Workflow Developers, Business Users, and Administrators) need a secure, intuitive, and robust way to register accounts, sign in, manage active sessions, and recover forgotten passwords. Without an email verification mechanism, malicious or mistyped email registrations can pollute the system. Furthermore, storing ephemeral one-time passwords (OTPs) in the relational database risks bloat and performance degradation, while relying on console logs or insecure mock codes compromises production security.

## Solution

A complete, production-grade Authentication and Authorization system for FlowPilot:
1. **Interactive Auth Modal**: Allows users to seamlessly toggle between Sign In, Sign Up, and Forgot Password directly within the application.
2. **Real-time Password Strength Meter**: Provides immediate visual feedback on password complexity (length, uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters) and confirms password match before submission.
3. **Redis-backed OTP Verification**: Implements a 2-step registration and password recovery flow. OTPs (6-digit numeric codes) are stored in Redis with an automatic 5-minute TTL (Time-To-Live) and deleted immediately upon successful verification, keeping the primary relational database completely clean.
4. **Real SMTP Email Delivery**: Sends beautifully formatted verification emails via Nodemailer with strict SMTP configuration, ensuring users receive their OTPs in their inbox without insecure UI autofill or debug log exposure.
5. **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Supports roles (`ADMIN`, `DEVELOPER`, `BUSINESS_USER`) embedded in signed JWT tokens, with user profile retrieval (`/me`) and secure session persistence.

## User Stories

1. As a Business User, I want to view an authentication modal from the navigation bar, so that I can easily sign in or register without losing my current page context.
2. As a Business User, I want to see real-time visual feedback on my password strength while registering, so that I can create a secure password that meets enterprise security standards.
3. As a Business User, I want immediate validation when my password confirmation does not match the entered password, so that I don't submit mismatched credentials.
4. As a Business User, I want to select my role (`DEVELOPER` or `BUSINESS_USER`) during registration, so that my account is assigned appropriate initial permissions.
5. As a Business User, I want to receive a 6-digit OTP in my email inbox upon submitting the registration form, so that I can verify that I own the email address.
6. As a Business User, I want the system to warn me if an email address is already registered before sending an OTP, so that I can choose to log in instead.
7. As a Business User, I want to enter my 6-digit OTP in a dedicated verification screen, so that my registration is completed securely.
8. As a Business User, I want the ability to request a new OTP if my current code expired or was not received, so that I am not permanently blocked from completing registration.
9. As a Business User, I want clear countdown and error messaging if an entered OTP is incorrect or expired, so that I understand why verification failed.
10. As a Business User, I want to log in using my registered email and password, so that I can access my workflows and account data.
11. As a Business User, I want my authentication session to persist across page reloads via a JWT token, so that I don't have to repeatedly re-authenticate.
12. As a Business User, I want to see my profile avatar, name, email, and role in the navigation bar when logged in, so that I know which account is active.
13. As a Business User, I want to securely log out with a single click, so that unauthorized persons cannot access my account on shared devices.
14. As a Business User, I want to initiate a "Forgot Password" flow by entering my email address, so that I can regain access to my account if I forget my credentials.
15. As a Business User, I want to receive a password reset OTP via email, so that only the email owner can reset the account password.
16. As a Business User, I want to enter the reset OTP along with my new password and confirmation, so that my password is updated in a single verified step.
17. As a Workflow Developer, I want to be automatically redirected or authorized based on my `DEVELOPER` role, so that I can access workflow design and debugging features.
18. As an Administrator, I want users' sensitive credentials to be stored as salted hashes (bcrypt) and ephemeral OTPs to be kept in memory-backed storage, so that the primary database remains clean, high-performing, and secure.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Architecture & Pattern**: The Monolith Backend follows Clean Architecture and CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation). The Auth feature is encapsulated into its own dedicated module, exposing clean commands and queries (`SendRegisterOtpCommand`, `VerifyOtpCommand`, `RegisterCommand`, `LoginCommand`, `RefreshTokenCommand`, `GetCurrentUserQuery`, `ForgotPasswordCommand`, `ResetPasswordCommand`).
- **Clean Architecture Email Decoupling**: The application layer depends on the `EmailService` domain abstraction (`libs/auth/src/domain/services/email.service.ts`). The infrastructure layer provides `NodemailerEmailService`, cleanly bound in `AuthModule`. Reusable HTML and plain-text email templates are generated via `EmailTemplateBuilder` rather than inline strings.
- **Storage Strategy for OTPs**: OTPs are strictly stored in Redis with a 5-minute TTL (`EX 300`). No OTP records are stored in PostgreSQL, and any legacy OTP relational tables have been removed. Keys are structured with domain namespaces (e.g. `otp:register:<email>` and `otp:reset:<email>`) and are automatically deleted upon successful verification.
- **Decoupled Verification**: A dedicated `POST /auth/verify-otp` endpoint validates OTPs and records verified status in Redis (`otp:verified:<type>:<email>`) with a 15-minute TTL, allowing flexible two-step registration and password reset workflows.
- **Refresh Token Mechanism**: 
  - `accessToken`: 15-minute expiration, containing `sub`, `email`, and `role`.
  - `refreshToken`: 7-day expiration, stored in Redis (`refresh_token:<REDACTED>`) with 7-day TTL.
  - `POST /auth/refresh`: Validates refresh token against Redis, verifies user active state, and issues a new access token and rotated refresh token.
- **Frontend HTTP Client Architecture**: 
  - Shared Axios instance (`frontend/src/shared/api/http-client.ts`) with request and response interceptors.
  - Request Interceptor: Reads `accessToken` from `auth.store` and automatically injects `Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>` on all requests.
  - Response Interceptor: Intercepts `401 Unauthorized` responses, calls `POST /auth/refresh` with `refreshToken`, replays failed requests with the new access token, and triggers `logout()` if refresh fails.
  - Migrated both `auth.api.ts` and `workflow.api.ts` to use this shared client.
- **Email Delivery Mechanism**: Transports OTP emails via real SMTP through `NodemailerEmailService`. Credentials (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM`) are loaded from environment variables. For local development, MailHog (`mailhog/mailhog:v1.0.1`) runs via Docker Compose on port 1025 (SMTP) and port 8025 (Web UI).
- **Password Security**: Passwords must meet minimum complexity criteria (minimum 8 characters, at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, 1 number, and 1 special character). Passwords are hashed using bcrypt with a salt round factor of 10 prior to persistence.
- **API Contracts**:
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/send-register-otp`: Validates uniqueness of email and dispatches a 6-digit OTP to the email address.
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-otp`: Accepts `{ email, otp, type }`, verifies OTP code in Redis, and marks email as verified for 15 minutes.
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/register`: Accepts name, email, password, role, and optional OTP. Checks verification status or verifies OTP, creates user in PostgreSQL, and issues both access and refresh tokens.
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/login`: Validates email and password, returning user details, `accessToken` (15m), and `refreshToken` (7d).
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`: Accepts `{ refreshToken }`, verifies against Redis, and returns a new token pair.
  - `GET /api/v1/auth/me`: Validates the Bearer <REDACTED> token and returns the current authenticated user's profile.
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password`: Checks user existence and dispatches a 6-digit password reset OTP to the email address.
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password`: Accepts email, OTP, and new password. Verifies OTP from Redis, updates the user's hashed password, and invalidates the OTP.

## Testing Decisions

- **Testing Seam Principle**: Tests must evaluate external behavior at the highest possible seams without testing internal implementation details or mocking CQRS internals.
- **Backend Testing Seam**: HTTP API Integration Tests on `apps/api` (`/api/v1/auth/*`). The test suite communicates directly via HTTP calls against running or test-instantiated NestJS application instances with real Redis and PostgreSQL test instances. Assertions verify:
  - HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 409).
  - JWT token validity, expiration, and payload contents.
  - Token refresh and rotation via `POST /auth/refresh`.
  - Redis key creation, TTL enforcement, and post-verification deletion.
  - User creation in PostgreSQL and password hash verification.
- **Frontend Testing Seam**: Component and user flow integration tests on `AuthModal`, `features/auth`, and Axios interceptors using React Testing Library. Assertions verify:
  - Switching between Login, Register, and Forgot Password modes.
  - Password strength validation bar changes color and width as characters are typed.
  - Form submission triggers OTP step and renders the 6-digit OTP input.
  - Zustand `auth.store` properly updates `user`, `token`, `refreshToken`, and `isAuthenticated` states.
  - Shared Axios interceptor intercepts 401 and calls refresh endpoint.

## Out of Scope

- Multi-factor authentication (MFA/TOTP) via authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy).
- Social / OAuth2 login providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft).
- Multi-tenant Organization/Team management (planned for post-MVP).

## Further Notes

- **MailHog Local Testing**: Run `docker-compose up -d mailhog` and view sent emails at `http://localhost:8025`.
- **Database Seeding**: `monolith-backend/prisma/seed.ts` does not run automatically on app start; it is executed manually via `npx prisma db seed`.
- Production deployments require valid SMTP relay credentials configured in environment variables (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM`).
- Redis service is managed via Docker Compose (`flowpilot-redis`).

3	## Problem Statement
4	
5	CrabFlowPilot needs a clear technical foundation before workflow-design and execution features can be developed safely. Without agreed product scope, module boundaries, a database model, and a reproducible local environment, later features would become tightly coupled and difficult to evolve.
6	
7	## Solution
8	
9	Establish the MVP foundation for a workflow-automation platform. The foundation defines the product boundary, adopts a modular-monolith architecture, provides the initial PostgreSQL schema, and prepares frontend, backend, Prisma, and local database tooling.
10	
11	## Scope
12	
13	### Included
14	
15	- Define the MVP scope and the principal product modules.
16	- Use a Modular Monolith backend with Clean Architecture and CQRS.
17	- Establish frontend and backend technology choices.
18	- Model workflow, draft, published version, connector, execution, and execution-log data in Prisma/PostgreSQL.
19	- Prepare PostgreSQL through Docker Compose and Prisma migrations.
20	
21	### Excluded
22	
23	- Distributed execution and multi-region deployment.
24	- Real-time collaboration.
25	- Connector marketplace and a large connector catalog.
26	- Full execution runtime, monitoring, and production CI/CD.
27	- AI workflow generation.
28	
29	## Architecture Decisions
30	
31	### Frontend
32	
33	- React 19, TypeScript, Vite, React Flow, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/base-ui.
34	
35	### Backend
36	
37	- NestJS, TypeScript, CQRS, Swagger, and Prisma ORM.
38	- Each business module is separated into Domain, Application, Infrastructure, and Presentation layers.
39	
40	### Database and Local Infrastructure
41	
42	- PostgreSQL is the primary relational database.
43	- Prisma owns the schema and migrations.
44	- Docker Compose provides the local PostgreSQL service.
45	
46	## Data Model Requirements
47	
48	The initial schema must support the following concepts:
49	
50	- `users` and roles.
51	- `workflows` as workflow metadata and ownership.
52	- `workflow_drafts` as one editable draft per workflow.
53	- `workflow_versions` as immutable published snapshots.
54	- `node_type_definitions` for node metadata and configuration schemas.
55	- `connectors` and `connector_credentials` for future integrations.
56	- `executions` and `execution_node_logs` for future runtime observability.
57	
58	## Acceptance Criteria
59	
60	- The project has documented product scope, architecture, and core data relationships.
61	- Frontend and backend applications can be started as separate applications.
62	- Prisma schema and migrations represent the core workflow domain.
63	- A local PostgreSQL instance can be started with Docker Compose.
64	- The database model keeps editable drafts separate from immutable published versions.
65

Status: resolved

## Problem Statement

CrabFlowPilot needs a clear technical foundation before workflow-design and execution features can be developed safely. Without agreed product scope, module boundaries, a database model, and a reproducible local environment, later features would become tightly coupled and difficult to evolve.

## Solution

Establish the MVP foundation for a workflow-automation platform. The foundation defines the product boundary, adopts a modular-monolith architecture, provides the initial PostgreSQL schema, and prepares frontend, backend, Prisma, and local database tooling.

## Scope

### Included

- Define the MVP scope and the principal product modules.
- Use a Modular Monolith backend with Clean Architecture and CQRS.
- Establish frontend and backend technology choices.
- Model workflow, draft, published version, connector, execution, and execution-log data in Prisma/PostgreSQL.
- Prepare PostgreSQL through Docker Compose and Prisma migrations.

### Excluded

- Distributed execution and multi-region deployment.
- Real-time collaboration.
- Connector marketplace and a large connector catalog.
- Full execution runtime, monitoring, and production CI/CD.
- AI workflow generation.

## Architecture Decisions

### Frontend

- React 19, TypeScript, Vite, React Flow, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/base-ui.

### Backend

- NestJS, TypeScript, CQRS, Swagger, and Prisma ORM.
- Each business module is separated into Domain, Application, Infrastructure, and Presentation layers.

### Database and Local Infrastructure

- PostgreSQL is the primary relational database.
- Prisma owns the schema and migrations.
- Docker Compose provides the local PostgreSQL service.

## Data Model Requirements

The initial schema must support the following concepts:

- `users` and roles.
- `workflows` as workflow metadata and ownership.
- `workflow_drafts` as one editable draft per workflow.
- `workflow_versions` as immutable published snapshots.
- `node_type_definitions` for node metadata and configuration schemas.
- `connectors` and `connector_credentials` for future integrations.
- `executions` and `execution_node_logs` for future runtime observability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The project has documented product scope, architecture, and core data relationships.
- Frontend and backend applications can be started as separate applications.
- Prisma schema and migrations represent the core workflow domain.
- A local PostgreSQL instance can be started with Docker Compose.
- The database model keeps editable drafts separate from immutable published versions.

3	## Problem Statement
4	
5	Users need a visual way to create and edit workflow graphs. Writing a workflow definition manually as JSON is error-prone and prevents business users from designing automations independently.
6	
7	## Solution
8	
9	Provide a Workflow Designer MVP built with React Flow. A user can create or open a workflow, compose a graph on a canvas, configure nodes, and automatically save the current draft.
10	
11	## User Stories
12	
13	1. As a user, I want to create a workflow before opening the designer, so that changes are associated with a workflow ID.
14	2. As a user, I want to load an existing workflow draft, so that I can continue editing it.
15	3. As a user, I want to drag nodes from a palette onto a canvas, so that I can build a workflow visually.
16	4. As a user, I want to move, connect, select, and delete nodes and edges, so that I can change the workflow graph.
17	5. As a user, I want to configure the selected node in a properties panel, so that each node can hold its required settings.
18	6. As a user, I want my changes to save automatically and see the saving state, so that I do not lose work.
19	
20	## Functional Requirements
21	
22	### Open Designer
23	
24	- Creating a new workflow calls `POST /workflows` before canvas interaction is enabled.
25	- Opening an existing workflow calls `GET /workflows/:id/draft` and maps the saved definition onto the canvas.
26	
27	### Canvas Operations
28	
29	- The node palette initially contains mock node types, including trigger and action examples.
30	- Users can drag nodes to the canvas, move them, connect them, select them, and remove nodes or edges.
31	- The designer stores a React Flow graph composed of `nodes`, `edges`, and `viewport`.
32	
33	### Node Configuration
34	
35	- The properties panel displays the selected node.
36	- Node configuration is stored in `node.data.config`.
37	- The MVP may use predefined configuration fields; future versions will generate forms from `node_type_definitions.config_schema`.
38	
39	### Autosave
40	
41	- Changes are debounced for approximately two seconds.
42	- The current graph is sent to `PUT /workflows/:id/draft`.
43	- The UI presents `Saving...` and `Saved` states.
44	
45	## Data Contract
46	
47	The draft definition follows this shape:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "nodes": [],
52	  "edges": [],
53	  "viewport": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "zoom": 1 }
54	}
55	```
56	
57	## Out of Scope
58	
59	- Authentication and authorization.
60	- Graph validation and publishing.
61	- Workflow execution and scheduling.
62	- Dynamic node catalog, connector credentials, and AI workflow generation.
63	
64	## Acceptance Criteria
65	
66	- A user can create a workflow and open the designer.
67	- A user can add, move, connect, select, configure, and delete canvas elements.
68	- Reloading a workflow restores its saved draft graph.
69	- Editing the graph triggers autosave and reports its state in the UI.
70	
71

Status: resolved

## Problem Statement

Users need a visual way to create and edit workflow graphs. Writing a workflow definition manually as JSON is error-prone and prevents business users from designing automations independently.

## Solution

Provide a Workflow Designer MVP built with React Flow. A user can create or open a workflow, compose a graph on a canvas, configure nodes, and automatically save the current draft.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to create a workflow before opening the designer, so that changes are associated with a workflow ID.
2. As a user, I want to load an existing workflow draft, so that I can continue editing it.
3. As a user, I want to drag nodes from a palette onto a canvas, so that I can build a workflow visually.
4. As a user, I want to move, connect, select, and delete nodes and edges, so that I can change the workflow graph.
5. As a user, I want to configure the selected node in a properties panel, so that each node can hold its required settings.
6. As a user, I want my changes to save automatically and see the saving state, so that I do not lose work.

## Functional Requirements

### Open Designer

- Creating a new workflow calls `POST /workflows` before canvas interaction is enabled.
- Opening an existing workflow calls `GET /workflows/:id/draft` and maps the saved definition onto the canvas.

### Canvas Operations

- The node palette initially contains mock node types, including trigger and action examples.
- Users can drag nodes to the canvas, move them, connect them, select them, and remove nodes or edges.
- The designer stores a React Flow graph composed of `nodes`, `edges`, and `viewport`.

### Node Configuration

- The properties panel displays the selected node.
- Node configuration is stored in `node.data.config`.
- The MVP may use predefined configuration fields; future versions will generate forms from `node_type_definitions.config_schema`.

### Autosave

- Changes are debounced for approximately two seconds.
- The current graph is sent to `PUT /workflows/:id/draft`.
- The UI presents `Saving...` and `Saved` states.

## Data Contract

The draft definition follows this shape:

```json
{
  "nodes": [],
  "edges": [],
  "viewport": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "zoom": 1 }
}
```

## Out of Scope

- Authentication and authorization.
- Graph validation and publishing.
- Workflow execution and scheduling.
- Dynamic node catalog, connector credentials, and AI workflow generation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can create a workflow and open the designer.
- A user can add, move, connect, select, configure, and delete canvas elements.
- Reloading a workflow restores its saved draft graph.
- Editing the graph triggers autosave and reports its state in the UI.

## Problem Statement

Define the initial execution-module boundary and the lifecycle of a node execution. This is a design and scaffolding effort only; no executable workflow runtime is included in this phase.

For each node, the future execution engine will:

1. Interpolate incoming data into node configuration.
2. Retrieve the required connector credential.
3. Run the node implementation.
4. Apply retry and error-handling policy when necessary.
5. Normalize the output for downstream nodes.
6. Persist execution and node-log data.

## Required Domain Concepts

- An execution references a specific published `WorkflowVersion`.
- An execution has an overall lifecycle and status.
- Each executed node produces a node log containing status, input, output, error, retry count, and timing information.
- Credentials are retrieved through the connector boundary rather than embedded in a workflow definition.

## Scope

### Included

- Define module responsibilities and directory structure.
- Define the node-execution lifecycle.
- Prepare the schema concepts for executions and node logs.

### Excluded

- Running workflow graphs.
- Queue processing, parallel execution, retry implementation, and timeouts.
- Connector runners and credential encryption implementation.
- Execution monitoring UI and workflow-log UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The project has a documented execution lifecycle and clear module boundary.
- The database model contains the concepts needed for executions and node logs.
- The Execution Module can be implemented later without redefining the workflow-version contract.

2	
3	## 1. Overview
4	The publish validation feature sits in the designer application layer (`monolith-backend/libs/designer`) and validates a workflow draft before creating an immutable `WorkflowVersion` snapshot.
5	
6	Validation is organized into three sequential layers:
7	1. **Existence validation**: Verifies workflow and draft exist and draft definition is non-empty.
8	2. **Catalog & Schema validation**: Resolves node keys via `node.data.key` (with fallback to `node.type`), fetches schemas via `GetNodeConfigSchemasQuery`, verifies catalog existence, and checks required config properties against `configSchema.required`.
9	3. **Graph structure & Reachability validation**: Verifies at least one trigger node exists, at least one action/processing node exists, and all action nodes are reachable from a trigger node through directed edges.
10	
11	## 2. Architecture & CQRS Integration
12	### Application Layer
13	- `PublishWorkflowCommand`: Dispatched with `workflowId` and `publishedById`.
14	- `PublishWorkflowHandler`: Orchestrates the validation and version snapshot creation.
15	- `GetNodeConfigSchemasQuery`: CQRS query dispatched to `@app/node-library` to fetch catalog metadata (`key`, `category`, `configSchema`) in a single batch query.
16	
17	### Domain Models
18	- `Workflow`: Root workflow entity. Updated with `currentVersionId` on publish success.
19	- `WorkflowDraft`: Stores canvas `definition` (`nodes[]`, `edges[]`) and `validationErrors`.
20	- `WorkflowVersion`: Immutable version record created upon passing validation.
21	
22	## 3. Node Resolution & Taxonomy
23	### Canvas Data Structure
24	React Flow stores nodes on canvas as:
25	```json
26	{
27	  "id": "actionNode-1792220527195",
28	  "type": "actionNode",
29	  "data": {
30	    "key": "ai.llm.generate",
31	    "name": "LLM",
32	    "config": {
33	      "provider": "gemini",
34	      "model": "gemini-3.5-flash-lite",
35	      "prompt": "..."
36	    }
37	  }
38	}
39	```
40	
41	### Key Resolution Helper
42	To support both production React Flow drafts and test fixtures:
43	```ts
44	const getNodeKey = (node: any): string | undefined => {
45	  if (typeof node?.data?.key === 'string' && node.data.key.length > 0) {
46	    return node.data.key;
47	  }
48	  if (
49	    typeof node?.type === 'string' &&
50	    node.type !== 'actionNode' &&
51	    node.type !== 'triggerNode'
52	  ) {
53	    return node.type;
54	  }
55	  return undefined;
56	};
57	```
58	
59	### Classification
60	- **Triggers**: Nodes where `nodeType.category === 'TRIGGER'` or `node.type === 'triggerNode'`.
61	- **Actions / Processing Nodes**: Nodes where `category !== 'TRIGGER'` and `node.type !== 'triggerNode'` (covers `LOGIC`, `DATA_PROCESSING`, `INTEGRATION`, `AI`).
62	
63	## 4. Graph Reachability Algorithm
64	1. Construct adjacency list: `adjacency: Map<string, string[]>` from `edges[].source` -> `edges[].target`.
65	2. Initialize `reachable: Set<string>` and queue with all trigger node IDs.
66	3. Traverse graph using BFS/DFS. Mark each visited node in `reachable`.
67	4. Iterate over all action nodes. If an action node ID is not in `reachable`, push `ACTION_UNREACHABLE` issue with `nodeId`.
68	
69	## 5. Schema Validation Algorithm
70	1. For each node, resolve `key = getNodeKey(node)`.
71	2. Look up `nodeType = nodeTypesByKey.get(key)`.
72	3. If not found in catalog, push `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE`.
73	4. If found, inspect `schema = nodeType.configSchema as { required?: string[] }`.
74	5. For each `field` in `schema.required`:
75	   - Inspect `value = node.data?.config?.[field]`.
76	   - If `value === undefined || value === null || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length === 0)`, push `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` with `nodeId` and `field`.
77	
78	## 6. Execution & Persistence Flow
79	1. If `issues.length > 0`:
80	   - Persist `{ issues }` to `draft.validationErrors`.
81	   - Throw `BadRequestException({ message: 'Workflow validation failed.', issues })`.
82	2. If `issues.length === 0`:
83	   - Clear `draft.validationErrors = null`.
84	   - Calculate next `versionNumber`.
85	   - Create and persist `WorkflowVersion`.
86	   - Update `workflow.currentVersionId` to the newly created version ID.
87	   - Return `{ versionId, versionNumber }`.
88

# Design: Workflow Publish Validation

## 1. Overview
The publish validation feature sits in the designer application layer (`monolith-backend/libs/designer`) and validates a workflow draft before creating an immutable `WorkflowVersion` snapshot.

Validation is organized into three sequential layers:
1. **Existence validation**: Verifies workflow and draft exist and draft definition is non-empty.
2. **Catalog & Schema validation**: Resolves node keys via `node.data.key` (with fallback to `node.type`), fetches schemas via `GetNodeConfigSchemasQuery`, verifies catalog existence, and checks required config properties against `configSchema.required`.
3. **Graph structure & Reachability validation**: Verifies at least one trigger node exists, at least one action/processing node exists, and all action nodes are reachable from a trigger node through directed edges.

## 2. Architecture & CQRS Integration
### Application Layer
- `PublishWorkflowCommand`: Dispatched with `workflowId` and `publishedById`.
- `PublishWorkflowHandler`: Orchestrates the validation and version snapshot creation.
- `GetNodeConfigSchemasQuery`: CQRS query dispatched to `@app/node-library` to fetch catalog metadata (`key`, `category`, `configSchema`) in a single batch query.

### Domain Models
- `Workflow`: Root workflow entity. Updated with `currentVersionId` on publish success.
- `WorkflowDraft`: Stores canvas `definition` (`nodes[]`, `edges[]`) and `validationErrors`.
- `WorkflowVersion`: Immutable version record created upon passing validation.

## 3. Node Resolution & Taxonomy
### Canvas Data Structure
React Flow stores nodes on canvas as:
```json
{
  "id": "actionNode-1792220527195",
  "type": "actionNode",
  "data": {
    "key": "ai.llm.generate",
    "name": "LLM",
    "config": {
      "provider": "gemini",
      "model": "gemini-3.5-flash-lite",
      "prompt": "..."
    }
  }
}
```

### Key Resolution Helper
To support both production React Flow drafts and test fixtures:
```ts
const getNodeKey = (node: any): string | undefined => {
  if (typeof node?.data?.key === 'string' && node.data.key.length > 0) {
    return node.data.key;
  }
  if (
    typeof node?.type === 'string' &&
    node.type !== 'actionNode' &&
    node.type !== 'triggerNode'
  ) {
    return node.type;
  }
  return undefined;
};
```

### Classification
- **Triggers**: Nodes where `nodeType.category === 'TRIGGER'` or `node.type === 'triggerNode'`.
- **Actions / Processing Nodes**: Nodes where `category !== 'TRIGGER'` and `node.type !== 'triggerNode'` (covers `LOGIC`, `DATA_PROCESSING`, `INTEGRATION`, `AI`).

## 4. Graph Reachability Algorithm
1. Construct adjacency list: `adjacency: Map<string, string[]>` from `edges[].source` -> `edges[].target`.
2. Initialize `reachable: Set<string>` and queue with all trigger node IDs.
3. Traverse graph using BFS/DFS. Mark each visited node in `reachable`.
4. Iterate over all action nodes. If an action node ID is not in `reachable`, push `ACTION_UNREACHABLE` issue with `nodeId`.

## 5. Schema Validation Algorithm
1. For each node, resolve `key = getNodeKey(node)`.
2. Look up `nodeType = nodeTypesByKey.get(key)`.
3. If not found in catalog, push `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE`.
4. If found, inspect `schema = nodeType.configSchema as { required?: string[] }`.
5. For each `field` in `schema.required`:
   - Inspect `value = node.data?.config?.[field]`.
   - If `value === undefined || value === null || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length === 0)`, push `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` with `nodeId` and `field`.

## 6. Execution & Persistence Flow
1. If `issues.length > 0`:
   - Persist `{ issues }` to `draft.validationErrors`.
   - Throw `BadRequestException({ message: 'Workflow validation failed.', issues })`.
2. If `issues.length === 0`:
   - Clear `draft.validationErrors = null`.
   - Calculate next `versionNumber`.
   - Create and persist `WorkflowVersion`.
   - Update `workflow.currentVersionId` to the newly created version ID.
   - Return `{ versionId, versionNumber }`.

1	# Feature Specification: Workflow Publish Validation
2	
3	## 1. Context
4	When a user publishes a workflow from the designer, the system must validate the draft before creating a new immutable workflow version snapshot. The goal is to ensure the workflow is both structurally valid and executable in practice.
5	
6	This feature prevents publishing broken workflows such as drafts without a trigger, drafts without executable steps, disconnected/unreachable nodes, or nodes with incomplete required configurations.
7	
8	## 2. Problem Statement & Canvas Data Model
9	In the FlowPilot designer, workflow drafts are constructed using React Flow:
10	- `node.type`: Specifies the React Flow canvas rendering component (e.g., `'triggerNode'`, `'actionNode'`).
11	- `node.data.key`: Represents the actual domain catalog key (e.g., `'trigger.manual'`, `'integration.google_sheet.readRows'`, `'logic.filter'`, `'data.aggregate'`, `'ai.llm.generate'`, `'integration.gmail.send'`).
12	- `node.data.config`: Contains user-configured property values for the node.
13	
14	Node types belong to categories defined in the catalog:
15	- `TRIGGER`: e.g., `trigger.manual`
16	- `LOGIC`: e.g., `logic.filter`
17	- `DATA_PROCESSING`: e.g., `data.aggregate`
18	- `INTEGRATION`: e.g., `integration.google_sheet.readRows`, `integration.gmail.send`
19	- `AI`: e.g., `ai.llm.generate`
20	
21	Validation must properly resolve domain catalog keys, query the catalog for `category` and `configSchema`, and ensure the draft is completely valid before publishing.
22	
23	## 3. Goals
24	### Primary goals
25	- Block workflow publishing when the draft definition is invalid.
26	- Properly resolve node types via `node.data.key` (with legacy fallback to `node.type` for mock tests).
27	- Ensure the workflow has at least one valid trigger node.
28	- Ensure the workflow has at least one action/processing node across all non-trigger categories (`LOGIC`, `DATA_PROCESSING`, `INTEGRATION`, `AI`).
29	- Ensure every action/processing node is reachable from at least one trigger node via directed edges.
30	- Validate that all required fields specified by each node type's `configSchema` are provided with non-empty values.
31	- Store structured validation issues on the draft for frontend display and return HTTP 400 with details.
32	
33	### Non-goals
34	- Full execution simulation with external service API calls.
35	- Deep runtime expression evaluation beyond static configuration schema validation.
36	
37	## 4. In-Scope Requirements
38	### Backend validation requirements
39	1. **Workflow & Draft Existence**: Workflow and workflow draft must exist and draft definition cannot be empty.
40	2. **Catalog Key Resolution**: Resolve the catalog key from `node.data.key` (or fallback to `node.type` if `node.data.key` is omitted).
41	3. **Trigger Requirement**: The graph must contain at least one trigger node (`category === 'TRIGGER'` or `node.type === 'triggerNode'`).
42	4. **Action Requirement**: The graph must contain at least one non-trigger action/processing node (`category !== 'TRIGGER'`).
43	5. **Node Catalog Verification**: Every node in the graph must exist in the node type catalog (`NodeTypeDefinition`).
44	6. **Config Schema Validation**: For each node, verify that all fields listed in `configSchema.required` exist in `node.data.config` and are not null, undefined, or empty strings.
45	7. **Graph Reachability**: Every non-trigger action node must be reachable from at least one trigger node via directed edges.
46	8. **Validation Issue Persistence**: On validation failure, persist issues in `workflow_drafts.validationErrors` and throw HTTP 400 with the structured issues. On success, clear any existing draft validation errors and create a new immutable `WorkflowVersion`.
47	
48	## 5. Validation Rules & Issue Codes
49	| Code | Severity | Trigger Condition |
50	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
51	| `NO_TRIGGER` | `error` | Workflow draft contains 0 trigger nodes |
52	| `NO_ACTION` | `error` | Workflow draft contains 0 non-trigger action/processing nodes |
53	| `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE` | `error` | Node catalog key is not found in `NodeTypeDefinition` catalog |
54	| `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` | `error` | A field listed in `configSchema.required` is missing, null, or empty string |
55	| `ACTION_UNREACHABLE` | `error` | An action/processing node cannot be reached from any trigger node |
56	
57	## 6. Acceptance Criteria
58	- Valid workflow drafts (such as `definition-saved.json`) publish successfully into a new `WorkflowVersion` snapshot and set `currentVersionId`.
59	- Drafts missing a trigger fail with `NO_TRIGGER`.
60	- Drafts with only a trigger fail with `NO_ACTION`.
61	- Drafts with unconfigured required fields fail with `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` indicating `nodeId` and `field`.
62	- Drafts with orphaned/unreachable actions fail with `ACTION_UNREACHABLE` indicating `nodeId`.
63	- Drafts with unknown node keys fail with `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE`.
64	- Stored validation errors are cleared when a valid workflow is successfully published.

# Feature Specification: Workflow Publish Validation

## 1. Context
When a user publishes a workflow from the designer, the system must validate the draft before creating a new immutable workflow version snapshot. The goal is to ensure the workflow is both structurally valid and executable in practice.

This feature prevents publishing broken workflows such as drafts without a trigger, drafts without executable steps, disconnected/unreachable nodes, or nodes with incomplete required configurations.

## 2. Problem Statement & Canvas Data Model
In the FlowPilot designer, workflow drafts are constructed using React Flow:
- `node.type`: Specifies the React Flow canvas rendering component (e.g., `'triggerNode'`, `'actionNode'`).
- `node.data.key`: Represents the actual domain catalog key (e.g., `'trigger.manual'`, `'integration.google_sheet.readRows'`, `'logic.filter'`, `'data.aggregate'`, `'ai.llm.generate'`, `'integration.gmail.send'`).
- `node.data.config`: Contains user-configured property values for the node.

Node types belong to categories defined in the catalog:
- `TRIGGER`: e.g., `trigger.manual`
- `LOGIC`: e.g., `logic.filter`
- `DATA_PROCESSING`: e.g., `data.aggregate`
- `INTEGRATION`: e.g., `integration.google_sheet.readRows`, `integration.gmail.send`
- `AI`: e.g., `ai.llm.generate`

Validation must properly resolve domain catalog keys, query the catalog for `category` and `configSchema`, and ensure the draft is completely valid before publishing.

## 3. Goals
### Primary goals
- Block workflow publishing when the draft definition is invalid.
- Properly resolve node types via `node.data.key` (with legacy fallback to `node.type` for mock tests).
- Ensure the workflow has at least one valid trigger node.
- Ensure the workflow has at least one action/processing node across all non-trigger categories (`LOGIC`, `DATA_PROCESSING`, `INTEGRATION`, `AI`).
- Ensure every action/processing node is reachable from at least one trigger node via directed edges.
- Validate that all required fields specified by each node type's `configSchema` are provided with non-empty values.
- Store structured validation issues on the draft for frontend display and return HTTP 400 with details.

### Non-goals
- Full execution simulation with external service API calls.
- Deep runtime expression evaluation beyond static configuration schema validation.

## 4. In-Scope Requirements
### Backend validation requirements
1. **Workflow & Draft Existence**: Workflow and workflow draft must exist and draft definition cannot be empty.
2. **Catalog Key Resolution**: Resolve the catalog key from `node.data.key` (or fallback to `node.type` if `node.data.key` is omitted).
3. **Trigger Requirement**: The graph must contain at least one trigger node (`category === 'TRIGGER'` or `node.type === 'triggerNode'`).
4. **Action Requirement**: The graph must contain at least one non-trigger action/processing node (`category !== 'TRIGGER'`).
5. **Node Catalog Verification**: Every node in the graph must exist in the node type catalog (`NodeTypeDefinition`).
6. **Config Schema Validation**: For each node, verify that all fields listed in `configSchema.required` exist in `node.data.config` and are not null, undefined, or empty strings.
7. **Graph Reachability**: Every non-trigger action node must be reachable from at least one trigger node via directed edges.
8. **Validation Issue Persistence**: On validation failure, persist issues in `workflow_drafts.validationErrors` and throw HTTP 400 with the structured issues. On success, clear any existing draft validation errors and create a new immutable `WorkflowVersion`.

## 5. Validation Rules & Issue Codes
| Code | Severity | Trigger Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NO_TRIGGER` | `error` | Workflow draft contains 0 trigger nodes |
| `NO_ACTION` | `error` | Workflow draft contains 0 non-trigger action/processing nodes |
| `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE` | `error` | Node catalog key is not found in `NodeTypeDefinition` catalog |
| `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` | `error` | A field listed in `configSchema.required` is missing, null, or empty string |
| `ACTION_UNREACHABLE` | `error` | An action/processing node cannot be reached from any trigger node |

## 6. Acceptance Criteria
- Valid workflow drafts (such as `definition-saved.json`) publish successfully into a new `WorkflowVersion` snapshot and set `currentVersionId`.
- Drafts missing a trigger fail with `NO_TRIGGER`.
- Drafts with only a trigger fail with `NO_ACTION`.
- Drafts with unconfigured required fields fail with `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` indicating `nodeId` and `field`.
- Drafts with orphaned/unreachable actions fail with `ACTION_UNREACHABLE` indicating `nodeId`.
- Drafts with unknown node keys fail with `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE`.
- Stored validation errors are cleared when a valid workflow is successfully published.

1	# Technical Design: Workflow Version Restore
2	
3	## 1. Kiến trúc tổng thể (Architecture Overview)
4	
5	Hệ thống tuân thủ **Modular Monolith** kết hợp **Clean Architecture** và **CQRS** ở Backend (NestJS), cùng kiến trúc **Feature-Based** ở Frontend (React 19, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query, Zustand).
6	
7	Tính năng khôi phục phiên bản thuộc bounded context:
8	- Backend: `libs/modules/designer` (quản lý workflow, draft, versions)
9	- Frontend: `src/features/workflow` (canvas, history, dialogs)
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 2. Thiết kế Backend (NestJS + CQRS + Prisma)
14	
15	```mermaid
16	sequenceDiagram
17	    autonumber
18	    actor User as Client (Frontend)
19	    participant Ctrl as WorkflowVersionsController
20	    participant CmdBus as CommandBus
21	    participant Handler as RestoreVersionHandler
22	    participant Repo as PrismaWorkflowRepository
23	    participant Prisma as PostgreSQL (Prisma $transaction)
24	
25	    User->>Ctrl: POST /api/workflows/:id/versions/:versionId/restore { strategy }
26	    Ctrl->>CmdBus: execute(RestoreVersionCommand)
27	    CmdBus->>Handler: handle(command)
28	    
29	    Handler->>Repo: findWorkflowWithDraftAndVersion(workflowId, versionId)
30	    Repo-->>Handler: { workflow, draft, targetVersion }
31	    
32	    Handler->>Prisma: $transaction([executeStrategy])
33	    alt Strategy: PUBLISH_THEN_RESTORE
34	        Prisma->>Prisma: Insert new WorkflowVersion (v_next from current draft)
35	        Prisma->>Prisma: Update WorkflowDraft (definition = targetVersion.definition)
36	    else Strategy: BACKUP_THEN_RESTORE
37	        Prisma->>Prisma: Insert new Workflow + Draft (clone from current draft)
38	        Prisma->>Prisma: Update WorkflowDraft (definition = targetVersion.definition)
39	    else Strategy: OVERWRITE
40	        Prisma->>Prisma: Update WorkflowDraft (definition = targetVersion.definition)
41	    end
42	    Prisma-->>Handler: Transaction Success
43	    
44	    Handler-->>Ctrl: RestoreResultDto
45	    Ctrl-->>User: 200 OK { success: true, data: { ... } }
46	```
47	
48	### 2.1. Domain Layer
49	- **Entities:**
50	  - `Workflow`: Entity gốc chứa thông tin metadata, owner, `currentVersionId`.
51	  - `WorkflowDraft`: Entity chứa bản nháp đang chỉnh sửa (`definition`, `updatedAt`).
52	  - `WorkflowVersion`: Value object/Entity snapshot bất biến (`versionNumber`, `definition`, `publishedAt`).
53	- **Domain Services / Policies:**
54	  - `VersionRestorePolicy`: Kiểm tra tính hợp lệ của phiên bản cần khôi phục (phải thuộc cùng workflow, không thể khôi phục phiên bản của workflow khác).
55	
56	### 2.2. Application Layer (CQRS)
57	- **Command:** `RestoreVersionCommand`
58	  ```typescript
59	  export class RestoreVersionCommand {
60	    constructor(
61	      public readonly workflowId: string,
62	      public readonly versionId: string,
63	      public readonly userId: string,
64	      public readonly strategy: RestoreStrategy,
65	      public readonly backupWorkflowName?: string,
66	      public readonly publishComment?: string,
67	    ) {}
68	  }
69	  ```
70	- **Handler:** `RestoreVersionHandler`
71	  - Điều phối quy trình nghiệp vụ:
72	    1. Kiểm tra quyền sở hữu / quyền chỉnh sửa của user.
73	    2. Lấy dữ liệu workflow, draft hiện tại và target version.
74	    3. Kiểm tra logic theo strategy đã chọn.
75	    4. Bọc toàn bộ các thao tác ghi DB vào `prisma.$transaction`.
76	    5. Trả về kết quả sau khi khôi phục thành công.
77	
78	### 2.3. Infrastructure Layer
79	- **Prisma Repositories:**
80	  - `PrismaWorkflowRepository`: Bổ sung method thực thi transaction khôi phục:
81	    ```typescript
82	    restoreVersion(params: {
83	      workflowId: string;
84	      targetVersion: WorkflowVersion;
85	      strategy: RestoreStrategy;
86	      userId: string;
87	      backupName?: string;
88	    }): Promise<RestoreResult>;
89	    ```
90	- Sử dụng Prisma transaction:
91	  ```typescript
92	  await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
93	    if (strategy === RestoreStrategy.PUBLISH_THEN_RESTORE) {
94	      // 1. Tính toán next version number
95	      const maxVersion = await tx.workflowVersion.aggregate({
96	        where: { workflowId },
97	        _max: { versionNumber: true },
98	      });
99	      const nextVersionNumber = (maxVersion._max.versionNumber ?? 0) + 1;
100	
101	      // 2. Tạo snapshot version mới từ draft hiện tại
102	      await tx.workflowVersion.create({
103	        data: {
104	          workflowId,
105	          versionNumber: nextVersionNumber,
106	          definition: currentDraft.definition,
107	          publishedById: userId,
108	        },
109	      });
110	    }
111	
112	    if (strategy === RestoreStrategy.BACKUP_THEN_RESTORE) {
113	      // Tạo workflow backup mới
114	      const backup = await tx.workflow.create({
115	        data: {
116	          name: backupName || `[Backup] ${workflow.name} - ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
117	          ownerId: userId,
118	          status: 'DRAFT',
119	          draft: {
120	            create: {
121	              definition: currentDraft.definition,
122	            },
123	          },
124	        },
125	      });
126	    }
127	
128	    // Luôn cập nhật lại bản nháp bằng targetVersion.definition
129	    return await tx.workflowDraft.update({
130	      where: { workflowId },
131	      data: {
132	        definition: targetVersion.definition,
133	        updatedAt: new Date(),
134	      },
135	    });
136	  });
137	  ```
138	
139	### 2.4. Presentation Layer
140	- **Controller:** `WorkflowVersionsController`
141	  - Endpoint: `POST /api/workflows/:id/versions/:versionId/restore`
142	  - Endpoint: `GET /api/workflows/:id/draft/status`
143	- **DTOs:**
144	  - `RestoreVersionDto`: Validate bằng `class-validator`:
145	    - `strategy`: `@IsEnum(RestoreStrategy)`
146	    - `backupWorkflowName`: `@IsOptional() @IsString()`
147	    - `publishComment`: `@IsOptional() @IsString()`
148	
149	---
150	
151	## 3. Thiết kế Frontend (React 19 + shadcn/ui)
152	
153	### 3.1. Cấu trúc thư mục (Feature-Based)
154	```text
155	frontend/src/features/workflow/
156	├── api/
157	│   ├── workflow-version.api.ts       # Gọi endpoint restore & version history
158	│   └── workflow-draft.api.ts         # Gọi endpoint draft status
159	├── components/
160	│   ├── VersionHistorySheet.tsx       # Sheet danh sách phiên bản (shadcn/ui)
161	│   ├── VersionItem.tsx               # Hiển thị từng phiên bản và nút 'Restore'
162	│   └── RestoreConflictDialog.tsx     # Modal cảnh báo chọn strategy (shadcn/ui)
163	├── hooks/
164	│   ├── useRestoreVersion.ts          # Mutation hook (TanStack React Query)
165	│   └── useDraftStatus.ts             # Query hook kiểm tra unpublished changes
166	└── store/
167	    └── designer.store.ts             # Đồng bộ state React Flow canvas
168	```
169	
170	### 3.2. Quản lý trạng thái (State Management)
171	1. **Kiểm tra trạng thái Draft:**
172	   - Khi người dùng click nút "Restore" trên một version cũ:
173	   - Hook `useDraftStatus` kiểm tra cờ `hasUnpublishedChanges` (so sánh dirty state từ Zustand store hoặc gọi API `GET /api/workflows/:id/draft/status`).
174	   - Nếu `hasUnpublishedChanges === false`: Gọi ngay mutation `restoreVersion` với strategy `OVERWRITE` (trải nghiệm liền mạch, không làm phiền người dùng).
175	   - Nếu `hasUnpublishedChanges === true`: Mở `RestoreConflictDialog`.
176	
177	2. **Cập nhật sau khi Restore thành công:**
178	   - TanStack React Query invalidates:
179	     - `['workflows', workflowId, 'draft']`
180	     - `['workflows', workflowId, 'versions']`
181	   - Zustand Store cập nhật lại `nodes`, `edges`, `viewport` trên canvas từ `response.data.definition`.
182	   - Hiển thị Toast thông báo thành công via `sonner` hoặc shadcn `toast`.
183

76	    5. Trả về kết quả sau khi khôi phục thành công.
77	
78	### 2.3. Infrastructure Layer
79	- **Prisma Repositories:**
80	  - `PrismaWorkflowRepository`: Bổ sung method thực thi transaction khôi phục:
81	    ```typescript
82	    restoreVersion(params: {
83	      workflowId: string;
84	      targetVersion: WorkflowVersion;
85	      strategy: RestoreStrategy;
86	      userId: string;
87	      backupName?: string;
88	    }): Promise<RestoreResult>;
89	    ```
90	- Sử dụng Prisma transaction:
91	  ```typescript
92	  await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
93	    if (strategy === RestoreStrategy.PUBLISH_THEN_RESTORE) {
94	      // 1. Tính toán next version number
95	      const maxVersion = await tx.workflowVersion.aggregate({
96	        where: { workflowId },
97	        _max: { versionNumber: true },
98	      });
99	      const nextVersionNumber = (maxVersion._max.versionNumber ?? 0) + 1;
100	
101	      // 2. Tạo snapshot version mới từ draft hiện tại
102	      await tx.workflowVersion.create({
103	        data: {
104	          workflowId,
105	          versionNumber: nextVersionNumber,
106	          definition: currentDraft.definition,
107	          publishedById: userId,
108	        },
109	      });
110	    }
111	
112	    if (strategy === RestoreStrategy.BACKUP_THEN_RESTORE) {
113	      // Tạo workflow backup mới
114	      const backup = await tx.workflow.create({
115	        data: {
116	          name: backupName || `[Backup] ${workflow.name} - ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
117	          ownerId: userId,
118	          status: 'DRAFT',
119	          draft: {
120	            create: {
121	              definition: currentDraft.definition,
122	            },
123	          },
124	        },
125	      });
126	    }
127	
128	    // Luôn cập nhật lại bản nháp bằng targetVersion.definition
129	    return await tx.workflowDraft.update({
130	      where: { workflowId },
131	      data: {
132	        definition: targetVersion.definition,
133	        updatedAt: new Date(),
134	      },
135	    });
136	  });
137	  ```
138	
139	### 2.4. Presentation Layer
140	- **Controller:** `WorkflowVersionsController`
141	  - Endpoint: `POST /api/workflows/:id/versions/:versionId/restore`
142	  - Endpoint: `GET /api/workflows/:id/draft/status`
143	- **DTOs:**
144	  - `RestoreVersionDto`: Validate bằng `class-validator`:
145	    - `strategy`: `@IsEnum(RestoreStrategy)`
146	    - `backupWorkflowName`: `@IsOptional() @IsString()`
147	    - `publishComment`: `@IsOptional() @IsString()`
148	
149	---
150	
151	## 3. Thiết kế Frontend (React 19 + shadcn/ui)
152	
153	### 3.1. Cấu trúc thư mục (Feature-Based)
154	```text
155	frontend/src/features/workflow/
156	├── api/
157	│   ├── workflow-version.api.ts       # Gọi endpoint restore & version history
158	│   └── workflow-draft.api.ts         # Gọi endpoint draft status
159	├── components/
160	│   ├── VersionHistorySheet.tsx       # Sheet danh sách phiên bản (shadcn/ui)
161	│   ├── VersionItem.tsx               # Hiển thị từng phiên bản và nút 'Restore'
162	│   └── RestoreConflictDialog.tsx     # Modal cảnh báo chọn strategy (shadcn/ui)
163	├── hooks/
164	│   ├── useRestoreVersion.ts          # Mutation hook (TanStack React Query)
165	│   └── useDraftStatus.ts             # Query hook kiểm tra unpublished changes
166	└── store/
167	    └── designer.store.ts             # Đồng bộ state React Flow canvas
168	```
169	
170	### 3.2. Quản lý trạng thái (State Management)
171	1. **Kiểm tra trạng thái Draft:**
172	   - Khi người dùng click nút "Restore" trên một version cũ:
173	   - Hook `useDraftStatus` kiểm tra cờ `hasUnpublishedChanges` (so sánh dirty state từ Zustand store hoặc gọi API `GET /api/workflows/:id/draft/status`).
174	   - Nếu `hasUnpublishedChanges === false`: Gọi ngay mutation `restoreVersion` với strategy `OVERWRITE` (trải nghiệm liền mạch, không làm phiền người dùng).
175	   - Nếu `hasUnpublishedChanges === true`: Mở `RestoreConflictDialog`.
176	
177	2. **Cập nhật sau khi Restore thành công:**
178	   - TanStack React Query invalidates:
179	     - `['workflows', workflowId, 'draft']`
180	     - `['workflows', workflowId, 'versions']`
181	   - Zustand Store cập nhật lại `nodes`, `edges`, `viewport` trên canvas từ `response.data.definition`.
182	   - Hiển thị Toast thông báo thành công via `sonner` hoặc shadcn `toast`.

FAILED : tiếp 108 loop mỗi item 109 R->>R: resolveConfig (prompt, system_prompt) 110 R->>X: executeItem({ config, item, credential }) 111 X->>Reg: get(config.provider) 112 X->>Ad: generate(request) 113 Ad->>API: HTTP (timeout 60s) 114 API-->>Ad: response / lỗi 115 Ad-->>X: { text, usage } / LlmProviderError 116 X->>X: retry nếu retryable (≤ 2) 117 X->>X: parse JSON nếu output_format = json 118 X-->>R: { text, data?, model, usage } 119 end 120 ``` 121 122 ### 3.1. Engine — hook giới hạn item (mở rộng `execution-item-model`) 123 Thêm vào `IPerItemExecutor`: 124 ```typescript 125 // Nhận config THÔ. Trả về số item tối đa node chấp nhận, null = không giới hạn. 126 maxItems?(rawConfig: Record): { limit: number; reason: string } | null; 127 ``` 128 `NodeRunner` (nhánh `per_item`), trước vòng lặp: 129 ``` 130 lim = executor.maxItems?.(rawConfig) 131 if lim && items.length > lim.limit: 132 FAILED, errorMessage = `Node received ${items.length} items, exceeds ${lim.reason}` 133 ``` 134 Hook dùng chung — node `per_item` tốn kém khác sau này dùng lại được. 135 136 ### 3.2. Domain (`libs/execution`) 137 ```typescript 138 export const NodeKeys = { /* ... */ AI_LLM_GENERATE: 'ai.llm.generate' } as const; 139 export const ConnectorKeys = { /* ... */ ANTHROPIC: 'anthropic', OPENAI: 'openai', GEMINI: 'gemini' } as const; 140 141 export const LlmLimits = { 142 DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS_CEILING: 100, // dùng khi không đặt env LLM_MAX_ITEMS 143 REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS: 60_000, 144 MAX_RETRIES: 2, 145 } as const; 146 ``` 147 148 ### 3.3. Application (`libs/execution`) 149 150 **Provider port:** 151 ```typescript 152 export interface LlmGenerateRequest { 153 model: string; 154 systemPrompt?: string; 155 prompt: string; 156 maxTokens: number; 157 temperature?: number; 158 outputFormat: 'text' | 'json'; 159 apiKey: ; 160 } 161 162 export interface LlmGenerateResult { 163 text: string; 164 usage: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number } | null; 165 } 166 167 export interface LlmProvider { 168 readonly key: string; // 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'gemini' 169 generate(request: LlmGenerateRequest): Promise; 170 } 171 172 export class LlmProviderError extends Error { 173 constructor(message: string, readonly retryable: boolean) { super(message); } 174 } 175 ``` 176 177 **`LlmProviderRegistry`:** map provider key → `LlmProvider`, inject qua token `LLM_PROVIDERS` (giống `NODE_EXECUTORS`). 178 179 **`LlmGenerateExecutor`** (`runMode: 'per_item'`): 180 - Constructor: `(registry: LlmProviderRegistry, maxItemsCeiling: number)`. 181 - `parseConfig` (zod v4): `provider` enum, `credential_id` uuid, `model` min(1), `prompt` min(1), `system_prompt` optional, `output_format` default `text`, `max_tokens` / `temperature` / `max_items` dùng `z.coerce.number()` (frontend cũ có thể gửi chuỗi) + default. 182 - `parseCredential`: `z.object({ api_key: })`. 183 - `expectedConnectorKey(raw)` → `raw.provider`. 184 - `maxItems(raw)` → `max_items` (đã coerce + default) so với `maxItemsCeiling`: 185 - `max_items ≤ ceiling` → `{ limit: max_items, reason: 'node max_items 50' }` 186 - ngược lại → `{ limit: ceiling, reason: 'platform limit LLM_MAX_ITEMS 100' }` 187 - `executeItem({ config, credential })`: 188 1. `adapter = registry.get(config.provider)` (thiếu → throw). 189 2. `result = callWithRetry(() => adapter.generate(request))` — retry khi `LlmProviderError.retryable`, tối đa `MAX_RETRIES`, backoff 1s → 2s. 190 3. Output `{ text, model: config.model, usage }` (usage đổi tên `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`). 191 4. `json` → `data = parseJsonOutput(text)`: bỏ code fence ```` ```json ... ``` ```` nếu có, `JSON.parse`; lỗi → throw `"LLM returned invalid JSON"`. 192 193 ### 3.4. Infrastructure (`libs/execution`) 194 Mỗi adapter implement `LlmProvider`, tạo client theo `apiKey` mỗi request, đặt timeout `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, **tắt retry nội bộ của SDK** (retry do executor quản lý), map lỗi → `LlmProviderError(retryable = status ∈ {408, 429} ∪ [500, 599] hoặc timeout)`. 195 196 | Adapter | SDK | JSON mode | Text | Usage | 197 |---|---|---|---|---| 198 | `AnthropicLlmAdapter` | `@anthropic-ai/sdk` | không có JSON mode riêng → thêm chỉ dẫn "Respond with valid JSON only" vào system prompt | ghép các content block `text` | `usage.input_tokens` / `output_tokens` | 199 | `OpenAiLlmAdapter` | `openai` | `response_format: { type: 'json_object' }` | `choices[0].message.content` | `usage.prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` | 200 | `GeminiLlmAdapter` | `@google/genai` | `responseMimeType: 'application/json'` | `response.text` | `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` / `candidatesTokenCount` | 201 202 `sanitizeErrorText` (engine) thêm pattern: `sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}`, `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}`, `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}`. 203 204 ### 3.5. Connector module (`libs/connector`) — CQRS 205 206 | Thành phần | Mô tả | 207 |---|---| 208 | `CreateApiKeyCredentialCommand(connectorKey, ownerId, name, apiKey)` + handler | Tìm connector active theo key; `authType !== API_KEY` → `BadRequest`; mã hoá `JSON.stringify({ api_key })` bằng `EncryptionUtil` + `ENCRYPTION_KEY`; lưu qua `ConnectorCredentialRepository.create`; trả DTO không có secret | 209 | `ListCredentialsQuery(connectorKey, ownerId)` + handler | `{ id, connectorKey, name, createdAt }[]` | 210 | `ConnectorsController` | `POST` / `GET /api/connectors/:connectorKey/credentials` (JWT, `@CurrentUser`) | 211 | `CreateApiKeyCredentialDto` | `name` `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty() @MaxLength(255)`, `api_key` `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty()` | 212 | `CredentialResponseDto` | map từ domain entity — không trả entity ra presentation | 213 214 ### 3.6. Module assembly 215 - `ExecutionModule`: đăng ký 3 adapter, `LLM_PROVIDERS`, `LlmProviderRegistry`; `LlmGenerateExecutor` qua factory đọc `LLM_MAX_ITEMS` (không hợp lệ / không đặt → `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS_CEILING`); thêm vào `NODE_EXECUTORS`. 216 - `ConnectorModule`: đăng ký command / query handler mới. 217 - `.env.example`: thêm `LLM_MAX_ITEMS=100`. 218 219 --- 220 221 ## 4. Frontend 222 223 ### 4.1. Cấu trúc 224 ```text 225 frontend/src/features/workflow/ 226 ├── api/credential.api.ts # GET/POST /api/connectors/:key/credentials 227 ├── services/credential.service.ts 228 ├── hooks/useCredentials.ts # useCredentials(connectorKey), useCreateApiKeyCredential() 229 ├── components/ 230 │ ├── PropertiesPanel.tsx # điều phối, chọn control theo schema 231 │ ├── config-fields/ 232 │ │ ├── CredentialField.tsx # OAuth (x-connectorKey) hoặc picker (x-connectorKeyFrom) 233 │ │ ├── EnumField.tsx # shadcn Select 234 │ │ ├── TextField.tsx # shadcn Input / Textarea (x-multiline), badge fx 235 │ │ └── NumberField.tsx # shadcn Input type=number → lưu number 236 │ └── AddApiKeyDialog.tsx # shadcn Dialog 237 └── types/node-type.ts # category thêm 'AI' 238 ``` 239 240 ### 4.2. Hành vi 241 - **Palette / Canvas:** `category` thêm `'AI'` (`node-type.ts`, `workflow.model.ts`); nhóm AI trong `Sidebar`; node AI render như action node. 242 - **`PropertiesPanel`:** tách render field ra `config-fields/*` (file < 200 dòng); chọn control theo thứ tự `x-refType` / `x-connectorKey` → `enum` → `integer | number` → `string`. 243 - **Kiểu giá trị:** `handleConfigChange(key, value: unknown)`; `NumberField` lưu `number` (rỗng → xoá key). 244 - **Credential picker (`x-connectorKeyFrom`):** 245 - Đọc `config[from]` (vd. `provider`); chưa có → disabled, gợi ý "Chọn provider trước". 246 - `useCredentials(provider)` → shadcn `Select`; mục cuối "+ Thêm API key" mở `AddApiKeyDialog`. 247 - Lưu thành công → invalidate `['credentials', provider]`, tự chọn credential vừa tạo. 248 - Đổi `provider` → xoá `credential_id`. 249 - **Gợi ý model:** lấy từ schema bằng hint `x-placeholderByField` (`{ field: "provider", values: { anthropic: "e.g. claude-opus-5-5", ... } }`), UI không hardcode. Chỉ là placeholder: model là text tự do, vì tên model đổi thường xuyên. Gợi ý của OpenAI và Gemini chưa được đối chiếu với danh sách model hiện hành. 250 - **Field OAuth hiện có (`x-connectorKey`)** giữ hành vi, thay `
